components.css: .ds-leg{display:flex;min-height:68px;width:420px;background:#fff;border:1.5px solid rgba(13,27,61,.78);border-radius:6px;box-shadow:0 1px 0 rgba(13,27,61,.14);overflow:hidden;transition:box-shadow .15s;font-family:Barlow,system-ui,sans-serif}.ds-leg:hover{box-shadow:0 10px 20px -16px rgba(13,27,61,.6)}.ds-leg-main{flex:1;padding:10px 16px}.ds-tab{display:inline-block;height:20px;line-height:20px;padding:0 6px;margin-right:8px;border-radius:3px;background:#8a5a00;color:#fff;font-family:'Barlow Condensed','Arial Narrow',sans-serif;font-weight:600;text-transform:uppercase;font-size:11px;letter-spacing:.1em}.ds-cap{font-family:'Barlow Condensed','Arial Narrow',sans-serif;font-weight:600;text-transform:uppercase;font-size:11px;letter-spacing:.14em;color:#69728f}.ds-title{margin-top:4px;font-size:15.5px;font-weight:500;color:#0d1b3d}.ds-meta{font-size:13px;color:#4a5578}.ds-meta b{font:700 12.5px 'JetBrains Mono',monospace;letter-spacing:-.02em}.ds-stub{width:92px;display:flex;flex-direction:column;align-items:center;justify-content:center;gap:4px;border-left:2px dashed #aeb5c8}.ds-d{font:700 18px 'JetBrains Mono',monospace;color:#4b2e83;letter-spacing:-.02em;font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums slashed-zero}

components.css: .ds-ticket{width:420px;padding-top:16px;background:#fff;border:1.5px solid rgba(13,27,61,.78);border-radius:6px;box-shadow:0 1px 0 rgba(13,27,61,.14);overflow:hidden}.ds-fare{margin:0 16px;display:grid;grid-template-columns:1.35fr 1fr .8fr;border-top:1.5px solid #0d1b3d;border-bottom:1.5px solid #0d1b3d}.ds-fare div{padding:8px 8px 8px 12px}.ds-fare div+div{border-left:1.5px solid #0d1b3d}.ds-fare div:first-child{padding-left:0}.ds-fare span,.ds-stubrow span{display:block;font-family:'Barlow Condensed','Arial Narrow',sans-serif;font-weight:600;text-transform:uppercase;font-size:11px;letter-spacing:.14em;color:#69728f}.ds-fare b{display:block;font:700 17px 'JetBrains Mono',monospace;color:#4b2e83;letter-spacing:-.02em}.ds-tear{position:relative;margin-top:16px;border-top:2px dashed #aeb5c8}.ds-tear::before,.ds-tear::after{content:'';position:absolute;top:-9px;width:16px;height:16px;border-radius:50%;background:#f2f2f0;box-shadow:inset 0 0 0 1.5px rgba(13,27,61,.78)}.ds-tear::before{left:-10px}.ds-tear::after{right:-10px}.ds-stubrow{padding:12px 16px 16px}.ds-urgent{font:700 44px/1 'JetBrains Mono',monospace;letter-spacing:-.05em;color:#d7262d}

components.css: .ds-stamp{display:inline-block;border:2.5px solid currentColor;border-radius:3px;padding:0 .45em;color:#d7262d;font:700 14px/1.35 'Barlow Condensed',sans-serif;letter-spacing:.16em;text-transform:uppercase;transform:rotate(-7deg);mix-blend-mode:multiply;animation:ds-stamp 420ms cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1) both}@keyframes ds-stamp{0%{transform:rotate(-14deg) scale(1.35)}60%{transform:rotate(-6deg) scale(.95)}100%{transform:rotate(-7deg) scale(1)}}@media (prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){.ds-stamp{animation:none}}

narrative.overview:
The semester is a carrier's ticket wallet. Every quiz, assignment and event is a coupon (a leg) printed on white stock and filed in a navy wallet; the wallet always shows what remains, and a finished leg is stamped USED rather than disappearing. The world borrows the jet-age airline ticket: navy carrier bars, condensed grotesk caps for every head and field label, ruled fare boxes, dashed tear lines with punched notches, a purple carbon-copy duplicate, and a rubber stamp. It is a vernacular-ephemera world, not a dashboard with a theme: there are no stat tiles and no generic cards, only coupons, stubs and copies.

Density is ticket-dense: small caps labels over bold mono figures, tight ruled rows, generous only around the one coupon that matters next. The phone is the primary surface: a navy top bar, the next-leg coupon owning the first viewport, a list of compact leg coupons, and a navy bottom tab bar. On desktop the navy rail replaces both bars and the next coupon sits beside its carbon copy.

Colour is functional and printed. Navy is the carrier (shell, rules, ink). Jet red is urgency and the one primary action. Carbon purple is the colour of every filled-in figure, as if the date, time, marks and D-count had been typed through carbon paper. Each course carries its own ink colour on a tab, like a flight number.
keyCharacteristics: Coupons with perforated D-count stubs are the unit of every list.
Condensed uppercase caps (Barlow Condensed) for heads, tabs and labels; Barlow for prose; JetBrains Mono carbon numerals for every figure.
Dashed tear lines with punched notches separate a coupon from its stub.
Done is a rotated jet-red USED stamp, never a removal or a green check.
Navy shell, white coupon stock on pale ticket-stock ground, lilac for the carbon copy.
Flat print: depth comes from 1.5px navy rules and a 1px ledge, not from floating shadows.

rules.name: The Carbon Figure Rule
rules.body: Every filled-in figure (date, time, marks, count, D-code) is JetBrains Mono bold in carbon purple with slashed zeros. A figure that turns urgent switches to jet red; a figure with no data goes ink-faint. Prose numbers stay in the body face.

rules.name: The One Red Rule
rules.body: Jet red marks urgency, the primary action, the active location and the stamp. It is never a decorative fill, a course colour or a card background.

rules.name: The Caps-Name, Sans-Say Rule
rules.body: Condensed caps name things (fields, places, courses, actions); Barlow carries sentences a person wrote. Never set a record title or description in caps, and never set a field label in sentence-case sans.

rules.name: The Twelve Floor Rule
rules.body: Labels sit at 11px minimum with wide tracking; body metadata at 13px minimum.

rules.name: The Drawn-Not-Lit Rule
rules.body: Containers are separated by navy rules and perforations, not by drop shadows. A shadow means the thing is floating or being hovered.

dos: Do build every list from coupons with a perforated stub (ticket rule, 6px corners, 1.5px navy).
Do set every figure in JetBrains Mono bold carbon purple with slashed zero; switch to jet red only when urgent.
Do mark finished work with the rotated USED stamp and keep it in the list.
Do open sections with the jet-red `///` mark, caps title and an optional carbon count.
Do put field labels in 11-12px condensed caps above their values, fare-box style.
Do separate a coupon from its stub with the notched tear line, notch fill matching the ground behind it.
Do keep motion to the three one-shot moves (print-in, stamp-in, slide-up) on the 0.16, 1, 0.3, 1 ease, all disabled under reduced motion.
donts: Don't reintroduce the slate-sidebar card dashboard with stat tiles this world replaced.
Don't use course ink for anything but its course tab and progress bar.
Don't use jet red decoratively or as a second accent fill.
Don't use the security-dot texture anywhere but empty states.
Don't separate containers with soft drop shadows; draw them with rules and perforations.
Don't set record titles or prose in uppercase caps.
Don't show a green check or remove a finished item instead of stamping it.
